requirements.text: The system shall read pipeline settings from config.yaml using a YAML reader utility in src/utils/common.py.

The AppConfiguration class (configuration.py) shall instantiate immutable ConfigEntity objects for each stage: DataIngestionConfig, DataValidationConfig, DataTransformationConfig, ModelTrainerConfig, ModelRecommendationConfig.
The Exception Handler module shall catch runtime exceptions, capture traceback details, and format structured error reports.

links.notes: captures file and line from the traceback

requirements.text: The component shall download raw zip archives containing BX-Books.csv, BX-Book-Ratings.csv, and BX-Users.csv from a remote GitHub storage URL specified in configuration.
requirements.notes: Downloads from the configured URL; if the download fails it generates a sample dataset (without BX-Users.csv) instead.

requirements.text: The system shall extract zip contents into artifacts/dataset/raw_data/.
Upon successful extraction, raw files shall be verified and moved to artifacts/dataset/ingested_data/.
requirements.notes: Presence of the raw CSVs is checked (sample data generated if missing); nothing is moved to ingested_data/.

links.notes: falls back to the check; no move

requirements.text: The system shall load BX-Books.csv and BX-Book-Ratings.csv.
User Filtering Rule: The component shall compute rating counts per user and discard users with fewer than 200 total ratings (ratings_count < 200).
requirements.notes: Threshold 200 from config, but if fewer than 50 rows survive it silently lowers the threshold to 5.

evidence.anchor_text: # Filter 1: Active Users (users with ratings count >= min_user_ratings)

requirements.text: Book Filtering Rule: The component shall compute rating counts per book title and discard books with fewer than 50 total ratings (ratings_count < 50).
requirements.notes: Threshold 50 from config, but if fewer than 5 books survive it lowers the threshold to 2.

evidence.anchor_text: # Filter 2: Frequently Rated Books (books with ratings count >= min_book_ratings)

requirements.text: The component shall perform an inner join on filtered users and filtered books to create the final cleaned ratings dataset.
Output files shall be saved to: artifacts/dataset/clean_data.csv, artifacts/serialized_objects/final_rating.pkl

evidence.anchor_text: # Save clean CSV and serialized final_rating.pkl

requirements.text: The system shall construct a pivot table where rows represent unique Book Titles (title) and columns represent unique User IDs (user_id).

evidence.anchor_text: # Create pivot table: rows=title, columns=user_id, values=rating

requirements.text: The system shall replace all NaN entries with 0 to populate missing user ratings.

The transformed pivot table and book title list shall be serialized to: artifacts/serialized_objects/book_pivot.pkl, artifacts/serialized_objects/book_names.pkl, templates/book_names.pkl (for Streamlit UI binding)
The component shall convert book_pivot into a Compressed Sparse Row matrix (scipy.sparse.csr_matrix).
The system shall initialize and fit a Scikit-Learn NearestNeighbors estimator with parameters: algorithm = 'brute', metric = 'cosine' (or Euclidean distance as defined in configuration)
The trained model instance shall be serialized and saved to artifacts/trained_model/model.pkl.
The engine shall deserialize model.pkl, book_pivot.pkl, and final_rating.pkl.
Given a input book title, the engine shall look up its row index in book_pivot.
The engine shall invoke model.kneighbors(..., n_neighbors=6) to retrieve the top 6 nearest neighbor indices (where the 1st neighbor is the query book itself).

evidence.anchor_text: # Find 6 nearest neighbors (1st neighbor is the query book itself)

requirements.text: For each of the top 5 recommended books, the engine shall query final_rating.pkl to extract the corresponding book image cover URL (Image-URL-L or Image-URL-M).
requirements.notes: URL column chosen in data validation (Image_URL_M, else Image_URL_L).

requirements.text: The engine shall return a dictionary/tuple list containing recommended titles and image URLs.
requirements.notes: Returns a tuple of two lists.

requirements.text: Book Selector Dropdown: Render a searchable dropdown populated with book titles from templates/book_names.pkl.
requirements.notes: Titles loaded by get_book_names(); the selectbox itself is module-level code (app.py:113-117).

requirements.text: Recommendation Button: Render a "Show Recommendation" button. Upon clicking: Compute recommendations using the Recommendation Engine. Display recommendations in a responsive 5-Column Layout. Show the cover poster image above each recommended book title.
requirements.notes: Button and 5-column layout are module-level code (app.py:122-141); the computation is RecommendationEngine.recommend.

requirements.text: Train Button: Render a "Train" trigger button allowing developers/admins to re-execute the ML Training Pipeline on demand.
requirements.notes: Sidebar button is module-level code (app.py:94-102) calling TrainingPipeline.run_pipeline.

links.notes: what the button runs; button is module-level app.py

requirements.text: Inference Latency: Real-time recommendation output shall be returned in under 500 ms after user selection.
Image Load Time: Poster images shall load directly from CDN/image URLs in under 1.5 seconds.
Model Training Execution: Pipeline training from Stage 0 to Stage 3 shall complete within 3 minutes on standard cloud VMs.
System Uptime: 99.5% availability when hosted on cloud container services (AWS ECS / Azure App Service).
Graceful Error Handling: If a book poster image URL is broken or missing, a default fallback placeholder image shall be displayed.
requirements.notes: Fallback used when the URL is missing or not http(s); a broken (unreachable) URL is not detected.

requirements.text: Modular Design: Pipeline stages are strictly decoupled. Modifying Stage 1 validation rules will not affect Stage 3 model fitting logic.
Configuration Driven: Hyperparameters (e.g., k=6, user rating threshold =200, book rating threshold =50) can be tuned directly via config.yaml without changing python source code.
requirements.notes: Thresholds, algorithm and metric come from config.yaml, but n_neighbors=6 is hard-coded in recommend() (the config value is unused).

requirements.text: Input validation on book search queries to prevent script injection.
requirements.notes: Selection is limited to dropdown values and recommend() checks the title exists, but titles are rendered with unsafe_allow_html (app.py:137); no injection protection.
